answer.rationale: The scenario is a clear-cut recordable work-related amputation with in-patient hospitalization, both of which trigger explicit, unambiguous OSHA recordkeeping obligations: the 24-hour reporting requirement for amputations/hospitalizations (§1904.39(a)(2)), the general recording criteria met by medical treatment/hospitalization (§1904.7(a)), the duty to record on the OSHA 300 log for covered employees (§1904.31(a), §1904.4(a)), and the 7-day entry requirement (§1904.29(b)(3)). No conflicting facts or missing predicates prevent a determinate answer given federal jurisdiction and same-day employer knowledge.
